summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, obstructive sleep apnea, asthma, and severe obesity, was admitted for acute on chronic left flank and low back pain following an attempted prednisone taper after a recent hospitalization. He reported that pain recurred when reducing prednisone below 60 mg and had self-managed with variable doses without relief. Initial evaluation included labs and spine imaging, which showed no acute fracture or infection, though white count was elevated consistent with steroid use or inflammation. The pain was managed with a restart of prednisone at 60 mg daily and a slow taper of 5 mg every three days, along with his baseline opioids and supportive medications. The chronic pain service recommended adding tizanidine and avoiding NSAIDs due to allergy history. Calcium, vitamin D, and Bactrim were prescribed for bone protection and infection prophylaxis given prolonged steroid use. The patient improved clinically, remained stable, and was discharged home with follow-up planned in the chronic pain clinic, while forgoing rheumatology re-engagement per his preference.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis of unspecified sites in spine
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Long term (current) use of systemic steroids
